## 59709a6b-6a0b-4fa1-95e7-9b9cba8cdeed / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** Experiment 2's fresh baseline (auto baseline, 120,832 completed steps, trained on target radii 0.14-0.20 m only) produced a stable late-training plateau; its leading measured policy, experiment-2 checkpoint-100352, scores 96.2% pooled research success (577/600: 195/200 seed 20000, 382/400 seed 21000) and 98.0% (196/200) on the reused task-reference panel, below the 98% objective. Experiment 3's full-range (0.06-0.20 m) fine-tune of that policy did not improve it: on a fresh shared 600-episode panel (seed 22000) the untouched parent scored 96.67%, and the two measured fine-tuned checkpoints scored 96.50% and 96.33%, with a near-identical failure set (19 of 23 union failures common to all three; at most 3 discordant episodes of 600). Across both experiments every recorded failure lies in the target-angle band about -116 to -156 degrees. A kinematic check of experiment 3's 20 failures shows that in this band the open-elbow inverse-kinematics solution requires a shoulder angle just beyond the -170 degree limit (|shoulder_open| 172-180 degrees), so only the folded-elbow branch is feasible; the folded solution places every joint within about 150 degrees, so the targets are reachable with kinematic margin. The residual is terminal precision, not reachability: successful episodes settle at a mean final distance of 0.34 cm, while the 20 failures settle at 1.0-2.2 cm after briefly approaching (13 of 20 entered the 1 cm tolerance only at steps 17-19 with max held 1-8 steps; 7 never entered). The deficit is thus not radial, not kinematic infeasibility and not training-distribution coverage; it is a branch-switch control/optimization limitation that concentrated training under the unchanged reward did not remove.

**Lessons and limits:** Reusable: measured task outcome, not training success_rate or ep_rew_mean, must select models (experiment 2's checkpoint-86016 held the run's maximum ep_rew_mean and 0.42 training success but measured 94.0%; experiment 3's transferred run began at success_rate 1.0 and never improved while measured success stayed flat). The late plateau is behaviorally homogeneous (zero discordant outcomes between leading experiment-2 checkpoints on shared panels; at most 3 of 600 across experiment-3 policies), so checkpoint selection inside a plateau is low-value. The task-reference panel is reused and selection-contaminated; its single 98.0% reading is one panel of 200 and is not independent confirmation. Limits: one training seed and one recipe lineage; only 7 checkpoints measured across the campaign; the folded-branch attribution is a kinematic feasibility computation plus a per-episode offset pattern, not a causal diagnosis of the policy's internal state, and the recorded diagnostics do not capture joint-limit contact, trajectories, or whether failures are static offsets or small limit cycles. The observation already exposes open- and folded-branch IK-angle errors, so branch information is present but evidently not exploited in this sector.

**Open questions:** Is the folded-branch terminal offset mainly an optimization/reward-shaping limitation (the current reward uses a 0.05 m closeness length scale, linear hold capital, and zero forfeit when a hold is lost) or a representation/control limitation of the 64x64 policy at the branch switch? Does the observation's infeasible open-branch error near the shoulder limit pull the policy toward the joint-limited posture instead of the feasible folded branch? Are the marginal failures static offsets or small limit cycles? Is the 98.0% task-reference reading a genuine level or one-panel variance? These are recorded uncertainties, not a queue of required actions.

working_lineage.reason: Experiment 4's reward reshape is contradicted and no experiment-4 checkpoint is competitive, so the working lineage remains the selected policy. On the fresh shared 600-episode panel seed 23000 the untouched transfer parent `working` (experiment-2 checkpoint-100352) scored 588/600 = 98.0% while experiment-4 checkpoints 100352 and 105472 scored 576/600 = 96.0% and 568/600 = 94.67%, and the parent won both paired comparisons (13 vs 1 and 21 vs 1 discordant episodes). The reshaped reward left the folded-branch band [-150,-120) unchanged (36/47 vs 37/47) and added reached-then-lost failures in bands the parent handles at 100%, so it degraded measured behavior rather than sharpening it. The working policy's genuine level is about 96.9% pooled over 1800 distinct research episodes (1745/1800), with every failure in the shoulder-limit folded-branch sector; the 98.0% seed-23000 and reused task-reference readings are favorable 200-600 episode samples. That pooled evidence is below the 98% objective and the residual is unchanged, so terminal assessment is not justified and request_final_benchmark is false.
